output:
**What I found:** Four of the stated rules break standard access-control rules. An editor handing out owner breaks attenuation. Checking an invitation only when it is sent skips the re-check at acceptance. "Any owner may leave" breaks the last-owner rule, and a denied provisioning call that leaves a row breaks "denial writes nothing." The tests must prove the corrected rules hold, not the rules as written. Nothing can be passed yet because the store and how it serializes writes aren't chosen (the record calls this DEFER).

**Why it matters:** Tests written to match the model as stated would lock in a privilege escalation, an owner-less workspace and orphaned user rows, and they would pass. Each corrected rule needs a test that the forbidden request is refused **and nothing was written**. A status-code check alone lets a half-done write through.

**Do this first:**
1. Have the product owner confirm the four corrected rules below replace the stated ones. Then write the rule-by-rule refusal tests and the random-sequence check against a pure access-decision function.
2. Follow-up: pick how the last-owner rule is enforced (`concurrency-control`), then write the two-owners-leave-at-once test against the real database.
3. Follow-up: count the disabled rows already left by denied provisioning calls, and plan their removal (`evolutionary-database-design`).

**What I did not check:**
- I read no code or tests in this repo, so this designs the tests rather than auditing existing ones. Closed by `Grep -i "invit|provision|owner"` over the source tree.
- No time limit is set for cancelling open invitations once a member's rights are removed. That's a decision for the owner, not something a command can close.

| Risk / criterion | Failure mode | Oracle | Technique | Scope / fidelity | Dependencies | Data / environment | Evidence | Residual blind spot |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Attenuation | An editor invites an owner or admin, or grants rights in a workspace they don't belong to | Every combination of inviter role and invited role above the inviter's own role is refused, and no invitation row exists | Decision table: inviter role × invited role × same/other workspace | The access decision as a pure function, plus one test through the invite endpoint that checks the store | Real store for the endpoint test | Fixtures per role, created fresh per test | None yet | Whether editors may invite at all, and at which roles (product decision) |
| Re-check at acceptance | An invitation still admits someone after the inviter was removed or demoted | Invite sent → inviter removed or demoted below the invited role → acceptance refused, no membership row created | State-transition tests over the invitation lifecycle | Accepting the invitation, against the real store | Real store; stub the email sender | Clock you can control for expiry | None yet | — |
| Revocation (follows from the re-check) | Removing a member leaves their open invitations usable | Removing a member cancels all their pending invitations within a declared time limit | State-transition | Member removal → list of pending invitations | Real store | — | None yet | The time limit is undeclared: **blocker** |
| Last owner | The sole owner leaves, or two owners leave or demote each other at the same moment → workspace has no owner | A leave or demote that would leave zero owners is refused; after a two-way race the workspace still has at least one owner | Negative test, plus an interleaving test of two concurrent requests | The real database at its production isolation level; a fake can't prove serialization | Real database | Two sessions with a barrier between them | None yet | How it is enforced (a conditional write on the owner count/version, or a serializable transaction) is not chosen yet |
| Denial writes nothing | A denied provisioning call leaves a disabled user, which later blocks the real user from being provisioned | After the denied call: zero user rows for that identity and one audit entry. A later allowed call for the same identity succeeds | Negative test plus a follow-up test that the identity still provisions | Provisioning endpoint against the real store; contract test on the identity provider's payload | Real store; recorded identity-provider requests | Identity values that don't collide across parallel runs | None yet | Disabled rows already in production |
| Grant model as a whole | Some sequence of steps lets an actor hold a right no chain of grants from an owner justifies, or leaves a workspace without an owner | Over random sequences of invite, accept, remove, demote, leave and provision: every right traces back to an owner; every workspace has at least one owner; refused steps leave state unchanged | Generative (property-based) test | Pure access-decision function, no store | None | Generated sequences with a fixed, logged random seed | None yet | Write races; the last-owner interleaving test covers those |

Handoffs:             concurrency-control (last-owner mechanism); evolutionary-database-design (remove existing disabled rows); defect-shift-left (generative test runs early, before integration tests); requirements-traceability (map each rule to its tests)
Residual risk:        time limit for revocation undeclared; editor invite scope undeclared; existing orphaned rows
